'''Yamashiro no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (also '''Yamashiro''' written as {{lang|ja|山代}} or {{lang|ja|山城}}; ''yamashiro no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''yamashiro kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled the southwestern part of {{ill|Yamashiro Province|ja|山城国}}.

== Overview ==
The name appears in three written forms: '''{{lang|ja|山背国造}}''', '''{{lang|ja|山代国造}}''', and '''{{lang|ja|山城国造}}'''.

=== Ancestry ===
*The "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'' records, in its account of rewards to meritorious retainers of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}, that '''{{ill|Amenomahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天目一箇神|lt=Amenomahitotsu-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=天目一命}}''' was appointed Yamashiro no Kuni no Miyatsuko.
*The same source records that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|lt=Jimmu|lt_ja=神武朝}}, '''Atane-no-Mikoto''' was appointed Yamashiro no Kuni no Miyatsuko, and that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu|lt_ja=成務朝}}, '''Sononofuri-no-Mikoto''' was appointed Yamashiro no Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Yamashiro clan|ja|山代氏}}''' (''yamashiro-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}). In Year 12 of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} ([[683]]), they were promoted to {{ill|Muraji|ja|連}}, and in Year 14, to {{ill|Imiki|ja|忌寸}}. Some members received the {{ill|Sukune|ja|宿禰}} kabane in Year 10 of {{ill|Tenchō|ja|天長}} ([[833]]).

== Base ==

=== Territory ===
The kuni no miyatsuko's territory was the region then known as '''Yamashiro Province''', later the western part of {{ill|Yamashiro Province|ja|山城国}} — present-day southern Kyoto Prefecture. In the north, the Yamashiro clan also lived in Ina-gō, Kawabe District of {{ill|Settsu Province|ja|摂津国}}.

== Tutelary deity ==
{{ill|Amenomahitotsu-no-Mikoto|ja|天目一箇命}}.

== People ==
*{{ill|Yamashiro-Neko-no-Mikoto|ja|山背根子命}}
*:Kuni no miyatsuko during the {{ill|regency of Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|lt=regency of Empress Jingū|lt_ja=神功皇后摂政期}}. Father of Hayama-hime, who at the empress's command founded {{ill|Hirota Shrine|ja|広田神社}}, and Naga-hime, who founded {{ill|Nagata Shrine|ja|長田神社}}.
